mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which typically leads to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, thereby driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following low UNRATE observations.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) crosses above 4.5%, it indicates tightening monetary conditions, which can lead to decreased borrowing and investment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the 5-day windows following FEDFUNDS crossing above 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 0.2% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5%, it signals strong labor market conditions, leading to increased consumer demand and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following the trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% month-over-month indicates increased economic activity, which can lead to higher corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following INDPRO growth above 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% month-over-month indicates strong demand in the housing market, which can lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following HOUST growth above 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real federal spending (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month indicates reduced government demand, which can lead to decreased economic activity and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the 20-day windows following RSAFS growth below -1%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5%, it indicates a tight labor market and potential monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the 5-day windows following the trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% quarter-over-quarter indicates strong economic growth, which can lead to increased corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following GDPC1 growth above 0.5%.
